title: Shape pin tests tie_dash_on in isolation, not its use inside draw_tie_mark — deleting the call site renders a solid ring with tests green
detail: The dashed-ring test only evaluates tie_dash_on(0..SEGS) directly; nothing pins that draw_tie_mark's loop actually consults it. Removing the `if !tie_dash_on(i) { continue }` guard yields a solid warning-shaped ring while all tests still pass.
recommended_fix: Pin the call-site linkage: e.g. factor the per-segment draw list into a pure proc (segments drawn vs skipped) and assert draw_tie_mark's segment set equals {i : tie_dash_on(i)}, or extract tie_dash_on's use into a testable enumeration the test consumes.

title: draw_tie_mark omits the degenerate-radius/alpha guard its own precedent draw_ring_annulus carries
evidence:
r := s * 0.62
	th := 2.5 * v.scale
	r_in, r_out := r - th * 0.5, r + th * 0.5
--- precedent spawn_fx.odin:385:
	if r_out <= 0 || r_in < 0 || col.a == 0 {
		return
	}
detail: draw_ring_annulus (the copied precedent) early-returns on r_out <= 0, r_in < 0, or col.a == 0; the new inline copy has no such guard, so a zero/negative-scale or transparent route_tie path draws degenerate/inverted triangles unguarded.
recommended_fix: Either call draw_ring_annulus per dash segment or replicate its `if r_out <= 0 || r_in < 0 || col.a == 0 { return }` guard at the top of the segment loop.
